tob-10812: J. Manning Potts gathers the prayers of medieval Christians — monks, nuns, kings, and ordinary believers — spanning a thousand years of devotion. tob-4012: David Hume was twenty-eight when he put out this bold bid to ground all knowledge in human experience. tob-4112: Griffith’s second Rigveda book crowns his trail-blazing verse-rendering — the later hymn-books, with the famed world-making hymn of book ten. plos-pone-0003412: Biochemists found that protein recipes are not random in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003512: Sleep researchers showed tired brains invent memories in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003612: Genomicists Wang and Leung found methylation's footprint in fish DNA in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003712: In 2008, Lee, Patel, and Christiani piloted a sepsis blood clue. plos-pone-0003812: Jiang, Bailey, and Goldman found blood stem cells moonlighting as lymphatic builders in this 2008 paper. Hematopoietic stem cells contributed to the lymphatic endothelium, the lining of the body's drainage vessels. The finding extends the blood stem cell's resume beyond blood.
plos-pone-0003912: In 2008, Nakano, Homae, and Watanabe caught sleeping babies' brains predicting sounds. plos-pone-0004012: In 2008, Shen, Sarin, and Liu raced sequencing platforms to find worm mutations. plos-pone-0004312: In 2009, Ambalavanan, El-Ferzli, and Roane tested a gentler gas delivery method. Inhaled nitric oxide delivered through an oxygen hood eased lung hypertension. The pilot trial offered a mask-free option for sick newborns. The simple approach could simplify bedside care greatly.
plos-pone-0352112: Why do travelers pick trains over planes or cars between cities? plos-pone-0357612: Immigrants face steep barriers to digital health services — language, trust, and access most of all. plos-pone-0357212: Traffic police command gestures must be readable by machines in any light. FDMB-YOLOv11 is a gesture recognition method built for varying lighting conditions. The robust model helps autonomous vehicles understand the officers directing them — a small but critical safety link.
plos-pone-0356612: What makes a social media post blow up? This paper predicted post popularity using multimodal deep learning, drawing insights from content features across text, image, and beyond. The models reveal which ingredients — and combinations — drive virality.
plos-pone-0357112: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper reporting indoor methane levels consistently above outdoor levels in homes with natural gas service. plos-pone-0356512: Plumbers face chemical, physical, and biological hazards that few study systematically. plos-pone-0355712: Measuring how well employees truly flourish at work needs validated tools — in every culture. plos-pone-0355312: Obesity passes from mother to child — especially in low-income households. This Malaysian convergent mixed methods study examined intergenerational obesity in poor families. plos-pone-0355612: Upper molars differ subtly between the sexes — measurably so. This cross-sectional study used geometric morphometrics to analyze maxillary molar sexual dimorphism. The findings refine forensic and anthropological sex estimation — teeth as identity documents.
plos-pone-0351112: Tracking objects in video — through occlusion and chaos — demands smarter transformers. This paper proposed an adaptive token division-based transformer for visual object tracking. The efficient architecture follows targets where conventional trackers lose them.
plos-pone-0354712: Wilms’ tumor — childhood kidney cancer — involves splicing gone awry. europmc-pmc2852312: Cracking protein shapes from scratch takes phasing tricks, and this 2010 paper demos a famed chain. The author shows SHELXC/D/E phasing joined to chain tracing and map honing. The combo turned hard cases easy. The write-up spread a pro workflow.
europmc-pmc2876112: The Asian tiger mosquito keeps marching, carrying dengue with it. This 2010 paper weighs what the expanding global range of Aedes albopictus means for dengue spread. The authors map the growing threat country by country. Their warning spurred mosquito watch programs worldwide.
europmc-pmc2885312: Active kids grow healthier, and this 2010 review stacks the evidence. The authors survey the health benefits of physical activity and fitness in school-aged children and youth. europmc-pmc3059412: Do stem cells feed or fight tumors? This 2011 review sifts studies on whether marrow stem cells help or hinder tumors. The authors weigh both sides fairly. Their review steadied a confused field. Context decides: wound signals tip the balance. The review remains a cited referee.
europmc-pmc3083512: Brain zaps' effects hinge on direction and timing. This 2011 paper shows tDCS polarity and timing shape motor learning results. The authors reveal the rules. Their work guides stimulation protocols. Anodal current helped; cathodal hindered. Clinics now time zaps with practice.
europmc-pmc6528712: Gallic acid is a plant compound found in fruits, tea, and medicinal herbs, credited with a long list of health effects. europmc-pmc6530612: Blood flow restriction training - lifting light weights with a cuff partially blocking blood flow to the muscle - builds strength surprisingly well. europmc-pmc6558212: The womb was long declared sterile - but bacterial DNA keeps turning up in first poop (meconium) and amniotic fluid. europmc-pmc6620612: After stroke, many survivors cannot use one arm - and recovery is slow. europmc-pmc6642112: Which cell types do disease genes act in? Combining single-cell RNA data with genome-wide association studies, researchers mapped complex traits onto their cellular homes. europmc-pmc6664112: Apoptosis - the cell's orderly self-destruct - keeps tissues healthy, and its failure feeds cancer. This review maps the apoptotic pathways and the drugs designed to push cancer cells back toward suicide. Targeting the death machinery remains a cornerstone of oncology.
europmc-pmc6678812: Deep inside mitochondria, a rare fat called cardiolipin glues the energy machinery together.
